title: Why Are Port Cranes So Gigantic?
description:
Almost everything you own crossed an ocean in a steel box, and every one of those boxes was lifted by a crane like this. A big ship-to-shore crane can weigh around two thousand tons, stand taller than a thirty-story building with its arm raised, and lift a box every couple of minutes, all day and all night. Today, ten parts of a port and its giant cranes, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:20 1. The arm that folds up
2:48 2. The height
4:21 3. The spreader
5:52 4. The corner holes
7:21 5. The cabin with a glass floor
8:45 6. The wheels and rails
10:03 7. Cranes that cross the ocean
11:23 8. The storm anchors
12:45 9. The rails inside the ship
14:10 10. The machine on stilts
15:25 The verdict

Sources:
- Malcom McLean and the Ideal X (1956, 58 containers): Wikipedia, "Malcom McLean" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcom_McLean
- Marc Levinson, "The Box: How the Shipping Container Made the World Smaller and the World Economy Bigger" (Princeton University Press, 2006)
- Ship-to-shore cranes, boom, outreach and spreaders: Wikipedia, "Container crane" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Container_crane
- Twistlocks and corner castings, ISO 1161 / ISO 668: Wikipedia, "Twistlock" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twistlock and "Intermodal container" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermodal_container
- Raising existing cranes for bigger ships: Port of Oakland, crane raising project https://www.portofoakland.com/
- ZPMC market share and 2024 US crane manufacturing plan: The White House fact sheet, 21 Feb 2024 https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2024/02/21/
- Typhoon Maemi (2003) crane collapses in Busan: Wikipedia, "Typhoon Maemi" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Maemi
- ONE Apus container loss (2020): Wikipedia, "ONE Apus" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ONE_Apus
- Cell guides and container lashing: Wikipedia, "Container ship" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Container_ship
- First automated terminal with AGVs (ECT Delta, Rotterdam, 1993): Wikipedia, "Automated guided vehicle" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_guided_vehicle
- Straddle carriers: Wikipedia, "Straddle carrier" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straddle_carrier
